title: GPU CI Supply-Chain Hardened Pipeline
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents the hardened CI/CD pipeline and acceptance criteria used to produce GPU runtime artifacts (images, kernels, quantized libs, and terraform modules) with supply-chain protections appropriate for production inference fleets. It is intended for infra engineers, release owners, and security reviewers responsible for GPU image and IaC delivery.

Scope:
- Builds and promotes GPU runtime images and kernel artifacts (x86/arm where applicable)
- Produces signed provenance metadata and attestation for air-gapped / private deployments
- Gates Terraform/IaC module promotions with deterministic validation harnesses
- Integrates egress/network tests and runtime telemetry smoke checks into the pipeline

Goals:
- Prevent unauthorized artifact injection (image/kernel/IaC)
- Ensure deterministic, reproducible builds for quantized kernels and runtime bundles
- Automate cryptographic signing and verification for promote gates
- Provide an explicit runbook for recovery and emergency rollback

High-level design:
1) Source provenance: all PRs must be merged via signed commits or a verified CI merge bot. The CI pipeline refuses builds when non-verified authors are present in the last 3 commits.
2) Deterministic build stage: use buildkit with fixed toolchain containers and pinned base images; record build inputs (git sha, package lockfile hashes, compiler versions).
3) Binary attestation: produce SLSA provenance (or equivalent) including SBOM (cyclonedx) and artifact signature (cosign).
4) IaC validation: run terraform plan/apply in a sandbox harness using simulated traffic and a drift detector before promote.
5) Promotion gate: signed artifact + passing integration tests + manual sign-off for major changes.

Pipeline stages (detailed):
- Stage A: Pre-flight checks (lint, dependency-scan)
  - Tools: tfsec, gosec, npm-audit (for node-based tools), trivy
  - Fail on high/critical CVEs in runtime/kernel dependencies

- Stage B: Deterministic build (buildkit + cache lock)
  - Inputs must include: Git SHA, GO/NCCL/CUDA versions, patchset id, Dockerfile digest
  - Outputs: image tarball, kernel .ko/.ptx, build-manifest.json

- Stage C: Unit & binary-level tests
  - Run unit tests for control-plane code and quick inference workflows with mocked KV cache
  - Run kernel unit tests in small emulation harness (QEMU or containerized GPU emulator where feasible)

- Stage D: Quantization & kernel validation
  - Run quantization toolchain with fixed seeds; calculate bit-level checksums of outputs
  - Compare against golden-reference set stored in artifacts-bucket (allowable delta policy documented below)

- Stage E: Integration (canary) in ephemeral cluster
  - Deploy image + IaC to ephemeral sandbox account/namespace
  - Run latency and tail-latency smoke tests (see SLOs below)
  - Run egress-path tests (NAT, proxy, privatelink) and validate metrics exported to synthetic-monitoring

- Stage F: Artifact signing and SBOM generation
  - Generate SBOM (cyclonedx), SLSA provenance, cosign signatures for image and tar artifacts
  - Store signatures and metadata in signed-artifacts-bucket parameterized by release tag

- Stage G: Promote to staging registry and run full-scale perf regression (nightly)
  - If perf regressions exceed policy, block promotion and open regression ticket

- Stage H: Manual review & production promote
  - For major kernel or IaC changes require at least two approvers from infra and security teams

Determinism policy and golden artifacts table:
| Artifact type | Determinism requirement | Acceptance check | Owner |
|--------------|-------------------------|------------------|-------|
| Kernel build (.so/.ptx/.ko) | Bit-identical across builds, or verified checksum delta policy | SHA256 match or documented delta <= 0.01% of floating ops | eng-serving-runtime |
| Docker runtime image | Reproducible layers ordering and manifest | Manifest digest matches signed manifest | eng-infra |
| Quantized weights | Stable numeric output with seeded quantizer | MSE against golden <= threshold (see appendix) | applied-ml |
| Terraform module | Deterministic plan given pinned provider versions | Plan hunk summary matches recorded golden plan | eng-infra/terraform |

Security controls and signing:
- Image and binary signing: cosign (public key pinned in vault). Keys are rotated quarterly.
- SBOM and provenance: cyclonedx + SLSA v1/v2 metadata embedded into artifact registry.
- Build isolation: builders run in ephemeral vaulted runners that wipe caches after successful sign-off.
- Least privilege: deploy service accounts are scoped per-stage; promotion service principal has MFA enforced.

CI gate checklist (automated + manual):
Automated checks (must pass):
- Dependency scan: no critical/high unaccepted CVEs
- Deterministic build: manifest present and checksums recorded
- SBOM attached and signed
- Integration smoke: tail-latency 95th < 150ms for canonical model on sandbox (configurable)
- Egress tests: outbound IPs and privatelink reachability verified

Manual checks (for major changes):
1) Release owner verifies provenance and review notes.
2) Infra lead confirms IaC plan delta is limited and safe for rollout.
3) Security reviewer checks SBOM and threat model for new high-risk dependencies.

Terraform/IaC interactions:
- Each runtime image promotion is accompanied by a module version bump when there are topology or runtime config changes.
- The pipeline executes terraform plan in a fully mocked network sandbox (VPC with replayed synthetic egress) and records the plan digest.
- For Private deployments: artifacts are exported as signed bundles with an install manifest that includes cosign signatures and sbom_url.

Validation harness details:
- Tooling: terratest, kitchen-terraform, a custom network-prober (go) that simulates 95th percentile client patterns.
- Resource constraints: ephemeral sandbox uses small GPU nodes (A10G-equivalent) and an ingress/egress proxy to emulate tenant traffic.
- Failure injection: network delay, NAT exhaustion, and spot-preemption simulated to validate graceful fallback.

SLOs and thresholds used in pipeline tests:
- 95th latency (inference) <= 150ms for canonical 512-token prompt
- 99th latency <= 400ms in sandbox integration
- No new critical CVEs accepted in dependency-scan stage
- Determinism checksum mismatch tolerance: 0 for kernels; 1e-4 relative MSE for quantized outputs

Promotion and rollback procedure (runbook):
1) On successful pipeline: artifacts pushed to staging and signed; notify release channel (#release-notify).
2) Nightly perf run passes for 3 consecutive runs -> automated promote to prod-registry (unless manual hold).
3) If post-promote regressions are detected (alert threshold exceeded), trigger emergency rollback:
   a) Run quick revert: tag previous signed artifact as active and trigger blue/green reroute
   b) If unsuccessful, run cluster rollback playbook: restore terraform state snapshot and redeploy previous module version
   c) Open postmortem and mark artifact as quarantined in registry

Owner and responsibilities:
- eng-infra: pipeline maintenance, staging registry, terraform harness
- eng-serving-runtime: kernel compatibility, perf regression triage
- applied-ml: quantization golden sets and numeric acceptance criteria
- security: review SBOMs, key rotation audits, and supply chain threat model

Oncall & emergency contacts:
- Primary: eng-infra oncall (pager)
- Secondary: eng-serving-runtime lead (Slack/Phone)
- Security escalation: security-ops@redwood.com

Appendix — common CLI snippets and examples:
- Verify cosign signature: cosign verify --key k8s://projects/my-project/secrets/cosign-key 
  ghcr.io/redwood/inference-runtime:2025.01

- Recreate deterministic build (local):
  git clone <repo> && git checkout <sha>
  docker buildx build --provenance=false --cache-from=type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/redwood/cache:latest -t local/runtime:sha
  sha256sum ./image.tar > local-manifest.txt

- Run terraform validation harness:
  make infra-sandbox && cd infra/sandbox && terraform init -get=false && terraform plan -var-file=ci.vars.tfvars > sandbox.plan

Appendix — exceptions and deltas policy:
- Low-severity CVEs with a documented compensating control may be accepted by Security-approved RFC; record the exception in the SBOM metadata and RFC index.
- For quantization deltas, a one-time golden-set rebaseline requires: applied-ml signoff + two infra approvers + nightly perf comparison for 5 days.
